cross_autocorr_s1 of cross_autocorr_s1, nested twice with ts_max and cs_last_high05: it is impossible to say what this measures. day_distinct_ratio(Ret) takes heavily tied k/n values, and the ordinal ranks inside cs_last_high05 break those ties by column order (trap 1).

The denominator of day_durbin_watson(Open) is an un-demeaned sum of squared prices, so the statistic is about intraday realized variance. The 30-day beta on day_last(Amt) is then divided by day_last(Amt) twice, so its scale is dominated by about 1/Amt^3. Vol x liquidity re-skin: liq 0.42, known family 0.39, 0.89 with #7.
Same construction as #6 with day_median(Volume) as the divisor. A 0.89 rewrite of #6; liquidity re-skin (liq 0.39, cap 0.43).

In the cross_regbeta the dependent variable day_wmean(Vwap,Open) is a back-adjusted price level (trap 3). The 60-day beta is a spurious-regression co-trend of price level and day_cov(Open,Ret), with scale near 1/vol and an unstable sign. No readable mechanism.

It is rank(LogFloatShares) passed through three cs_last_high40 screens. With direction -1 the long book is a fixed float-share band (about the 60-70th percentile) among names with low day_q_stat_std. A share-count re-skin (trap 2) with meaningless nested screens.

cross_reg_tvalue with x=pow_2_5(day_last(Amt)), which is about 1e10-1e20 in float32. In rolling_ols, t=beta/(se+1e-9) and se is far below 1e-9, so the 't' is really beta*1e9 and scales as 1/sd(Amt^2.5). A synthetic check confirmed t==beta/EPS exactly. When the last-minute amount is above roughly 3e7, var_x overflows to inf and the value is exactly 0. The cross-sectional rank is about sign(corr) x illiquidity: a numeric artifact and a liquidity re-skin.
